extraction.name: LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data
extraction.description: LUMA is a unique multimodal dataset featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes, specifically designed for learning from uncertain data. It extends the well-known CIFAR-10/100 dataset with audio samples extracted from three audio corpora, and text data generated using the Gemma-7B Large Language Model (LLM). The dataset includes 101,000 images, 135,096 speech audio recordings, and 62,875 text passages, amounting to approximately 3 GB of data. LUMA enables controlled injection of varying types and degrees of uncertainty and is available as a Python package including functions for generating multiple variants of the dataset with controlling the diversity of the data, the amount of noise for each modality, and adding out-of-distribution samples.
extraction.creator: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, Sébastien Fournier
extraction.citeAs: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Fournier. 2025. LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data. In Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR '25), July 13–18, 2025, Padua, Italy. ACM, New York, NY, USA, 10 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3726302.3730302
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was compiled from three modalities: (1) Images were sourced from CIFAR-10/100 datasets, supplemented with EDM Diffusion-generated images for diversity control. (2) Audio samples were extracted from three audio/text parallel corpora: The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice, using forced alignments to extract pronunciations of CIFAR class labels. Additionally, 73 recordings from colleagues were voluntarily contributed, anonymized, trimmed, and added. (3) Text passages were generated using the Gemma-7B Instruct LLM using 13 different prompts per class label.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Audio samples that failed automatic validation (transcription did not match class label) were sent for manual validation. Classes with fewer than 600 validated samples after alignment were designated as out-of-distribution (OOD) data rather than in-distribution training/test data. Samples with conflicting annotations during manual validation were rejected.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images: CIFAR-10/100 dataset and EDM Diffusion-generated images. Audio: The Spoken Wikipedia corpus, LibriSpeech corpus (derived from LibriVox audiobooks), Mozilla Common Voice corpus (crowdsourced), and 73 voluntary colleague recordings. Text: Generated by Google's Gemma-7B Instruct model using 13 different prompts per class label.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio samples were extracted using forced alignments (Montreal Forced Aligner for LibriSpeech and Mozilla Common Voice; phoneme-level alignments for Spoken Wikipedia). Plural forms of class labels were considered for audio extraction. For text, bias reduction for classes 'man', 'woman', 'boy', and 'girl' was achieved by reconstructing prompts to explicitly include topics and keywords with occupations. Label noise injection reassigns labels to the nearest class based on deep feature representations (Wav2Vec for audio, BERT for text, VGG-11 for images). Sample noise injection applies modality-specific noise: background noise from ESC-50 for audio, nlpaug-based noise for text, and Hendrycks & Dietterich perturbations for images.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio: Automatic validation using OpenAI's Whisper Large V3 model for transcription; samples where transcription matched the class label (or plural form) were accepted. Remaining samples were manually validated. 42 classes with more than 600 validated samples were used as in-distribution data; 8 classes with fewer were used as OOD data. Text: Generated texts were validated by masking label occurrences and feeding masked text back into Gemma-7B Instruct for classification; samples where the prediction matched the ground truth label were accepted (55,953 total). Bias detection was performed using Gemma model; biased texts were filtered for classes 'man', 'woman', 'boy', 'girl'. Images: 42 classes chosen to have at least 600 samples per class per modality after alignment; 8 classes with fewer samples used as OOD data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual audio validation was performed for samples that failed automatic validation and belonged to classes with fewer than 800 samples. Annotators were shown the audio sample with the prompt 'Is the audio saying the word below? (An extra s or es in the pronunciation is okay.)' with answer options 'Yes' or 'No'. Samples where both annotators confirmed validity were accepted; samples with conflicting annotations were rejected. For text bias detection, the Gemma model was asked to identify if the given text contains gender, racial, religious, or cultural biases.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 71.61% annotation agreement was achieved for audio manual validation. Only samples where both annotators agreed on validity were accepted (5,027 samples). Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected. For bias detection, the Gemma model was used but the authors note they are unable to assess how accurate or consistent these detections truly are.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 annotations per audio sample for manual validation
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 17 annotators consisting of M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors with advanced to fluent English knowledge
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OpenAI Whisper Large V3 (automatic audio transcription/validation), Gemma-7B Instruct (text generation and bias detection), Montreal Forced Aligner (forced alignment for LibriSpeech and Mozilla Common Voice), Wav2Vec (deep feature extraction for audio), BERT (deep feature extraction for text), VGG-11 (deep feature extraction for images)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available on HuggingFace (https://huggingface.co/datasets/bezirganyan/LUMA) and as a Python package on GitHub (https://github.com/bezirganyan/LUMA). The authors plan to include dependent modalities in the future. The open-source nature of the data compilation pipeline and code facilitates integration of new contributions from the community.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: 73 audio recordings were voluntarily contributed by colleagues and were anonymized before inclusion in the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to promote and support the development, evaluation, and benchmarking of trustworthy and robust multimodal deep learning approaches, particularly for safety-critical applications such as healthcare and autonomous driving. The authors anticipate that LUMA will help the research community design more trustworthy and robust machine learning approaches.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Gender bias was identified in text passages for classes 'man', 'woman', 'boy', and 'girl', with examples of stereotypical descriptions generated by the LLM. The Gemma model was used to detect gender, racial, religious, and cultural biases. Prompts for these 4 classes were reconstructed to minimize bias by including occupation-related keywords. The authors acknowledge that the dataset may contain factual inaccuracies or biases since textual data was generated using an LLM trained on unbalanced data. Audio data from forced alignments may contain misaligned segments introducing additional noise. Some audio samples from voluntary contributions may be very noisy or have strong accents.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may contain factual inaccuracies or biases in the text modality due to LLM generation. LUMA shall not be used as a source of knowledge or information. Audio samples from forced alignments may have misalignment noise. The bottleneck for diversity control is the number of audio samples (around 70% of 42 in-distribution classes have more than 900 audio samples). The dataset currently lacks dependent modalities. Text bias detection accuracy using the Gemma model cannot be fully assessed for consistency.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and benchmarking of multimodal deep learning models under uncertainty. Specifically designed for: (1) benchmarking multimodal uncertainty quantification methods; (2) studying aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty under controlled conditions; (3) out-of-distribution detection research; (4) evaluating model robustness to noise across modalities; (5) studying the interaction of uncertainties across modalities. The dataset supports controlled injection of varying types and degrees of uncertainty for tailored experiments.
